summary: You sit bottom of the table on 79 points, so your GW4 claims process first if these players are still free when the window runs (waivers close 11 September). Dropping to three claims this week: Garner, last night's drop candidate, is now confirmed set to start for Everton against Man Utd (Hackney a doubt with a knock), so the Ampadu swap is off - the rest of the defense and midfield (Munoz, Milenkovic, Bijol, Gvardiol, Collins, Schade, Tavernier) are all confirmed starters, and where the model still rates one of them low (Munoz next5 just 7.0) that looks like the model not yet pricing in his confirmed starting role rather than a real weakness. The three that still stand: Igor Jesus for Marmoush - Solanke's ankle injury (out since August, a major doubt) has actually lifted Marmoush's own standing, but Igor Jesus is a confirmed, in-form #1 striker for free, so the upgrade case is now about superior output rather than a bench risk. Le Fee for Barcola remains live - Barcola is still expected to start on the bench for his Liverpool debut tonight, while Le Fee is a confirmed Sunderland starter. Rayan for Doku is carried as a low-confidence hedge given Doku's calf return is edging closer.

claims.why: Igor Jesus is confirmed as Nottingham Forest's first-choice striker under new manager Oliver Glasner, ahead of Chris Wood, and Forest have started the season well. Marmoush's own case has actually improved since last night - Tottenham's Dominic Solanke has an ankle injury and hasn't played since early August, a major doubt this weekend, so the competition that clouded Marmoush's spot has eased and he is named in Tottenham's predicted XI at Forest on Friday. This is now a value upgrade (a confirmed #1 striker for free) rather than a bench-risk argument, so confidence is medium rather than high.
claims.model: Model has Igor Jesus at next5 14.5 (avail 0.95) versus Marmoush at 5.6 (avail 0.35) - a large model gap, but Marmoush's real avail looks higher than 0.35 now that Solanke is injured, so the true gap is smaller than the model shows; still worth the swap for Igor Jesus's superior nailed-on output.

claims.why: Barcola is still expected to start on the bench for his Liverpool debut against Ipswich tonight - manager Iraola has not ruled him in, and the latest predicted XI (published this morning) leaves him out of the starting eleven with Gakpo continuing on the left. Le Fee is a confirmed Sunderland starter in an attacking midfield role, so this is a straightforward swap of a bench-bound marquee name for a nailed starter while Barcola finds his feet.
claims.model: Model has Le Fee at next5 16.3 (avail 1.00) versus Barcola at 1.5 (avail 0.10) - the model has no career data on Barcola yet so it is essentially guessing zero, and tonight's team news supports that low number for now.

claims.why: Doku remains out with the calf injury picked up in the Community Shield, with a return pegged for around this gameweek, so this is a hedge rather than a certainty - if he returns to full training this week the claim is worth pulling. Rayan is a confirmed Bournemouth starter and this season's breakout midfield find, so he is a reasonable free-agent floor while Doku's exact return date is unclear.
claims.model: Model has Rayan at next5 16.2 (avail 0.95) versus Doku at 3.4 (avail 0.00) - the model already has Doku's injury priced in, so this claim is mostly about timing his eventual return rather than disputing the model.

claims.why: Woltemade left Newcastle for Juventus on a season-long loan on deadline day, so he plays in Serie A, not the Premier League, until at least next summer - a mandatory drop, not a judgement call. Igor Jesus is confirmed as Forest's starting striker in their predicted XI for Friday's game against Tottenham.
claims.model: Model: Igor Jesus next5 14.5 vs Woltemade 0.3, +14.2. Fully agree - the loan has pushed Woltemade's number to essentially zero, the clearest drop in the squad.

Gross is a fully fit, nailed-on Brighton starter with no fitness question at all. Only use this claim if you want the safer floor rather than Garner's upside.
